title: A Decadal Assessment of PM2.5 Pollution in Dhaka, Bangladesh (2015–2024): Pollution Severity, Temporal Variability, and Meteorological Associations
content: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a persistent air-quality problem in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and its severity and temporal variability calls for a long-term assessment. The present study reviewed PM2.5 pollution between 2015 and 2024 and investigated the seasonal, interannual, and meteorological correlation. Daily air-quality and meteorological data were analysed with descriptive statistics, air-quality benchmark comparison, general linear model, Spearman correlation and linear regression for three monitoring stations. A total of 7,943 station-day observations were processed, with 6,268 having good daily PM2.5 observations. Annual mean concentrations varied from 77.24 μg/m³ in 2017 to 108.74 μg/m³ in 2021, well above the annual guideline of 5 μg/m³ set by the World Health Organization. The concentrations differed significantly between seasons (p < 0.001) with higher levels found in winter season compared to monsoon season. The general linear model also indicated an interannual difference (p = 0.033), but no significant linear trend was observed by the linear regression (p = 0.797). Bivariate correlations were negative for temperature, relative humidity and wind speed, but none of these variables were statistically significant in the adjusted model. The findings indicate persistently high PM2.5 concentrations and pronounced seasonal variation. To improve air quality in Dhaka, sustained emission controls, uniform monitoring and coordinated air quality management is required.
